newsitem.title: USA: Herbalife to register CEO's shares.
newsitem.headline: Herbalife to register CEO's shares.

text.p: Herbalife International Inc said on Friday it expects to file with the Securities and Exchange Commission to register up to 4.6 million common shares owned by chief executive Mark Hughes.

The company said Hughes plans to use the shares to back notes, known as DECS, that are exchangable into Herbalife common. He plans to sell the notes, providing liquidity for a portion of his holdings, it explained.
In a separate statement, the company said that it expects to meet or exceed its expectations for 1996 financial results.

Although the audit for the year is not complete, the company said its preliminary numbers indicate that it will meet or exceed its expectations for financial results for the year. Full-year results are expected to be released in the third week of February.
Herbalife said it was commenting on expected 1996 results at this time due to unusually heavy trading volume in the company's stock in recent days.
The company cautioned the transaction planned by Hughes is not final and is subject to a number of contingencies.

It said Hughes may transfer the stock being registered to the DECS investors at the maturity of the DECS -- about three years following issuance -- although Hughes will retain an option to settle the transaction in cash and retain the shares.
Until the maturity date of the DECS, Hughes will continue to exercise voting rights over the shares, the company said.
As a result, he continues to exercise voting control over a majority of the shares of the company.
It said Hughes indicated his goals in the proposed offering are to enhance his estate's financial diversification and to address increasingly complicated estate and tax planning considerations.
The proposed transaction would involve one-quarter or less of the Herbalife shares held by Hughes, who will continue as the company's largest shareholder, it pointed out.
This transaction will have a non-dilutive effect, as no additional shares are being issued and no proceeds will be received by the company.
